claim: Enrollment occupies roughly 61% of the elapsed calendar time of a median industry phase III trial, which is the trial-level Amdahl ceiling on what perfect recruitment could buy.
source_title: RLSX Agent F derived calculation
authors_or_org: RLSX Agent F

figures.metric: enrollment duration as share of phase III elapsed duration
figures.denominator_def: median recruitment months divided by median completed phase 3 study length in months, same 2016-2019 window
figures.sample: see input evidence IDs

derivation: 18 months median recruitment [E-5001] / ((882+864+921.5+937)/4 = 901.125 days = 29.61 months) [E-5011] = 0.608. NOTE: the two medians come from different samples (E-5001 restricts to industry phase III drug trials with usable recruitment dates, n=606; E-5011 covers all completed phase 3 registrations), so this is an order-of-magnitude bound, not a within-sample ratio.

claim: Perfect recruitment could remove between about 25% and 61% of clinical-phase elapsed time, or roughly 15% to 36% of a 10.5-year total development timeline: eliminating phase III enrolment alone saves 1.55 of 6.25 years of sequential clinical elapsed time (24.8%); applying the same 61% enrolment share to all three phases saves 3.80 years (60.8%).
source_title: RLSX Agent F derived calculation
authors_or_org: RLSX Agent F

figures.metric: Amdahl ceiling for recruitment as a share of clinical elapsed time
figures.denominator_def: enrolment months removed divided by sequential clinical elapsed months
figures.sample: see input evidence IDs

derivation: Clinical elapsed = phase1 368.75 d + phase2 983.5 d + phase3 929.25 d = 2281.5 d = 6.25 yr (2018-2019 medians) [E-5011]. Lower bound: 0.608*929.25 = 565 d = 1.55 yr; 1.55/6.25 = 24.8%; /10.5 yr total = 14.7%. Upper bound: 0.608*2281.5 = 1387 d = 3.80 yr; /6.25 = 60.8%; /10.5 = 36.2%. Only phase III recruitment duration is directly measured; the upper bound assumes the same share in phases I and II.
